name: team_planning_capacity
description: Get the capacity of a scenario of a Team Planning plan the caller is in. Each person is a seat, and so is each position for the FTE its occupants leave open. Each place a seat holds (a unit or a position, and its share of the seat) is priced by the capacity model its role chooses through the capacity_model planning rule, a role's choice beating its family's. A place in a position takes the position's role and level; a person placed straight in a unit takes those their title and level map to. An allocation the HRIS didn't give (allocation_known false) shares what the seat's other places leave. Each figure carries its working. Totals are per model, per unit and for the scenario, never summed across models; a place in a unit gone from the map counts for the scenario only. A place no model covers counts nowhere and is listed in `unclassified` with its reason. Each working step has an op (+, × or =) and, where it charges for someone or an open seat, a subject_id. A figure is overloaded when what the seat costs to manage beats its base, by `excess`, and its notes say what a reader should know, such as an open seat that counts against no manager. A planner's override (team_planning_set_capacity_override) replaces a place's capacity, its working ends with the override, and `calculated` carries the model's figure, with that figure's overloaded, excess and notes in `calculated_diagnostics` while the top-level ones describe the planner's figure. An override the plan can't read, since its person was forgotten, leaves the place unclassified with the model's figure still in `calculated`. `overridden` marks every place the plan holds an override for, so one on a place that counts nowhere for another reason, such as a leaver's, stays visible. Figures are decimal strings. Each total carries `parts`, which add up to it per model: actual is the baseline's capacity (the baseline's figure, not actual pay), planned is what the plan's changes add or take away (negative where they take away, so someone moved between units is negative in the old unit and positive in the new), and forecast is what the plan's forecast assumptions add, zero until a forecast rule is set. The baseline is all actual. `units` lists each unit on the scenario's map that counts in any part, so a unit everyone left still shows its negative planned; a unit gone from the scenario's map counts in the scenario's parts only. `models` maps each model a place or a figure uses to its symbol, what follows its figures on screen, and its description. People are named by id, and `names` maps each to a name. An archived plan carries archived_on, priced_on and a note: its figures use the pay bands, exchange rates, budget lines and rules as they stood on priced_on, its archive day, while framework roles and levels are read as they are now. A plan archived before that copy was kept has no priced_on, and its figures use today's. Restoring a plan prices it with today's again. Refused, as an unknown plan, unless the caller is a member.

scenario_id.description: The scenario, or the plan's id for the baseline.
